activities.anchor: That third option is the profession this lesson defines.
activities.caption: three people will listen — pair each with what they give
activities.name: counsListenersMatch

config.prompt: Pair each listener with what they actually give:

pairs.right: loyalty, not skill — advice bends toward the friendship
answers from doctrine — the price is your agreement
trained listening, accountable to published evidence and ethics codes — the goal is explicitly your judgement, not their compliance

config.why: The listening is trained, the method is accountable, and the aim is your own judgement — that is what separates the profession from goodwill.

activities.caption: which word of the definition carries which claim?
activities.name: counsDefSort

config.prompt: Each claim belongs to one word of the definition — file it:

items.label: the most replicated finding of psychotherapy research — alliance quality predicts outcome
the client, not the counsellor, is the expert on and agent of their own life
bounded by ethics codes, accredited graduate training, supervised hours, state licensure
trust, agreement on goals, agreement on how to pursue them

config.why: Every word is load-bearing: the mechanism, the direction, the guarantee.

activities.anchor: Underneath the definition sits a philosophical commitment that makes counselling distinctive among the helping professions
activities.caption: two questions about one person — drag the divider
activities.name: counsWellnessCompare

config.prompt: Two questions about one person — drag the divider:

before.label: the medical model
before.text: asks 'what disorder is present and how is it treated?'

after.label: the developmental view
after.text: asks 'what does this person need to grow, and what is already working?' — distress as a normal part of life to be worked through with support and skill

config.why: That centre decides the spectrum: school guidance, career work, couples, grief, addiction, licensed treatment of clinical disorders.

config.q: Who walks into a counsellor's office?
choices: People across the whole spectrum — career decisions, grief, couple transitions, life stress, and yes, clinical disorders
Only people with a diagnosed mental illness
Nobody — counselling is self-help done alone
config.why: The centre is wellness- and development-oriented — the wait-until-unwell reading mistakes the whole point.

activities.anchor: clients disclose their worst fears, their crimes, their fantasies and their crises to a person they may have met three times
activities.caption: find the faulty line — confidentiality's fine print
activities.name: counsConfidentialSpot

config.prompt: One of these confidentiality claims is wrong — click it:
lines: Confidentiality is the foundation of the alliance.
Its limits are stated openly in informed consent, before work begins.
The legally mandated limits: risk of serious harm to self or others, suspected abuse of children or vulnerable adults, and court orders.
The duty of confidentiality dissolves the moment any unlawful act is mentioned.
Tarasoff (1976) converted a philosophical dilemma into every practitioner's legal landscape.
config.correction: The legally mandated limits are the named ones — serious harm to self or others, suspected abuse, court orders; ordinary disclosures stay protected.
config.why: The stakes are direct — which is why the limits are stated up front, in informed consent.

activities.anchor: protects the client's continuity and the worker's accountability
activities.caption: when a case pushes at the edges — the process
activities.name: counsEthicsOrder

config.prompt: When a case pushes at the edges of the rules — the process, in order:
items: Check the code and the law
Consult — the profession's quiet safety net
Document the reasoning and the outcome
config.why: Each rule guards a specific failure mode; the sequence exists because genuine goods collide more often than good meets evil.

activities.anchor: Ignoring it damages the alliance the treatment runs on
activities.caption: the 11 p.m. text — walk the response
activities.name: counsTextBranch

config.root: 11 p.m. A client texts — not a crisis, only a small message that isn't really about the message.

choices.label: Answer warmly and chat — rapport above all
choices.feedback: It erases the line, sets an unworkable precedent and quietly opens an unmonitored side-channel.

choices.label: Hold the agreed boundary and redirect to the scheduled channel
choices.feedback: Warm, brief, by the book — the informed-consent conversation set this policy up front.

chat.text: The precedent writes itself into every future night — the line is not a wall against care; it is a load-bearing part of it.

choices.label: Treat what the text was really saying as clinical material
choices.feedback: Exactly: the text was data, not noise — what it was really about gets the attention it asked for.

choices.label: Never mention it — off-hours stays off-topic
choices.feedback: Leaving it unaddressed frays the very relationship the work depends on.

material.text: Policy up front, boundary held warmly, message heard in session — settled by design, not instinct.

ignore.text: The small text still happened — unaddressed, it erodes exactly the trust the work is built on.

config.why: The line is not a wall against care; it is a load-bearing part of it.
